title: Return Core returns the whole of one received core row
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user. That role holds every permission, including Part sales -> Create & Edit and Invoicing & payments -> Create & Edit.
  2. A test customer exists. If not: Customers -> New Customer, enter a name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and save.
  3. A test vendor exists to order parts from. If not: Parts -> Vendors -> New Vendor, enter a Name (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Parts Supply"), then Save & Close.
  4. Start a new part sale today (a sale started before this release handles cores the old way): Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale, then select the customer.
  5. On the Parts tab click Add Part: Description "Water Pump", Quantity 10, Vendor = the test vendor, Sell Price $517.55, Core Charge $79.99. Save the row.
  6. In the Actions column click Order and confirm (all 10 are ordered).
  7. Click Receive; in the Receive parts dialog change the quantity to 6 and confirm. 4 are still owed.
custom_steps:
1. On the Parts grid, read the core rows and the quantity on the received core row.
  2. On that core row, click Return Core and look for any option to return only part of the row (e.g. 3 of the 6).
  3. Complete the return and read what was returned.
  4. Receive the remaining 4, then read the core rows again and look for Return Core on the new row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The 6 received arrive as their own received row with their own core row of 6.
  • Return Core on that row returns all 6; there is no way to return only part of one row.
  • When the 4 still owed arrive, they get their own core row of 4 with its own Return Core.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 5 Oct 2026 (specification edited that day). Source-verified 5 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R10: “Each delivery of a special-order part arrives as its own received row with its own core row, exactly as on a service work order: 10 ordered and 6 received gives a core row of 6, and Return Core on it returns those 6”
  • S1-R10: “A return covers the whole quantity of one received core row”
  • S1-R10: “Within one row there is no way to return part of it”
  • S1-R10: “The 4 still owed get their own core row, and their own Return Core, when they arrive”
